issuers.sector: Polymer compounds for wires, cables and pipe coating
issuers.headline: A profitable, cash-generative polymer compounder doubling capacity, priced at 34.5x FY26 earnings after the issue against a 14.5x peer median; our fair value is Rs 81 (Neutral) against Rs 150, because growth in the core manufactured business has been flat and the price already pays for the expansion.
red_flags: Operating EBITDA margin 5.5% -> 9.7% -> 12.0% FY24-26 (14.5% in Q1 FY27); PAT Rs 7.52 cr -> Rs 27.01 cr; cumulative CFO 118% of PAT (pp. 85-86)
Capacity to rise from 35,251 to 87,301 MTPA (+148%) by FY28 from Rs 77.56 cr of proceeds; current utilisation 73-75% (pp. 123-124)
Manufactured revenue flat to lower (Rs 254 cr -> Rs 237 cr FY24-26); growth came from resin trading, 31.9% of FY26 revenue (pp. 33, 406, 408)
Top customer 31.7% of FY26 revenue; top supplier 71.7% of procurement; purchases from promoter-group trader Vinsul Makardi 9.3% of revenue (pp. 27, 39, 89)
At Rs 150: P/E 34.5x post-issue vs peer median 14.5x (DDev Plastiks 13.0x, Kingfa 46.3x); reported P/E is a fair measure (earnings-quality adjustments -2.8%)
Fair value Rs 68 / 81 / 96 (Bear / Neutral / Bull) vs Rs 150; objects floor Rs 98; issuer KPI EBITDA leaves other income in (Rs 46.60 cr vs Rs 41.90 cr operating)

issuers.sector: Defence electronics: electro-optic and thermal imaging systems
issuers.brlm: JM Financial Limited; IIFL Capital Services Limited
issuers.headline: A leading Indian thermal-imaging OEM that owns its technology, priced at 78.8x FY26 earnings against an 85.6x peer median; our Neutral fair value is Rs 515 (-26% vs Rs 700) because FY26 was a down year with cash tied up in orders, and the outcome turns on how quickly the Rs 432 cr of orders convert.
red_flags: Owns 100% of its IP; largest supplier of thermal imaging to Indian government agencies Apr-24 to Mar-26 (issuer-paid F&S report, pp. 246, 253)
EBITDA margin 26.2% / 29.7% / 28.9% FY24-26 and cash tax 23.3% of PBT (pp. 89, 144)
Orders of Rs 432 cr in hand (Rs 314 cr book at Jun-26 plus Rs 118 cr won Jul-Sep), about 1.2x FY26 revenue (p. 250)

FY26 revenue -22.7% as export orders slipped; reported P/E 78.8x is flattered by a Rs 18.84 cr warranty write-back and Rs 34.17 cr of capitalised development (adjusted FY26 P/E 247.5x; three-year average 75.6x) (pp. 23, 351, 373)
Priced at 78.8x FY26 EPS and 7.2x book vs peer medians 85.6x and 13.0x (pp. 141, our computation)
Fair value Rs 486 / 515 / 556 (Bear / Neutral / Bull) vs Rs 700; QIB book 293.6x at close (NSE)

issuers.headline: Revenue doubled and PAT rose 6.3x over FY24-FY26 with cash tax fully paid, but operating cash flow was negative each year as inventory grew; at the Rs 147.33 pre-IPO reference the P/E (15.6x) is in line with peers.
red_flags: Revenue CAGR 41.9% and PAT CAGR 151.7% (FY24-FY26); cash tax 26.9% of PBT
Operating cash flow negative each year; cumulative CFO/PAT -87.5%
Volume sold +1.7% while revenue per kg +97.9%: growth price-led
Top-10 customers 22.32% of revenue; top-5 suppliers 56.98% of COGS
Post-issue P/E ~15.6x at reference vs peer median 15.72x
Related party Aalishaan: 5.06% of FY26 sales; subsidiary from Apr-26

issuers.headline: Revenue rose 2.5x over FY24-FY26 to Rs 106.76 cr with PAT of Rs 13.38 cr, but operating cash flow was negative in two of three years, 83.6% of revenue comes from ten customers, and the Rs 155.03 cr of identified objects imply a price of at least Rs 44.29 against Rs 17.50 in the last secondary transfers.
red_flags: Revenue Rs 41.87 cr to Rs 106.76 cr FY24-FY26 (2.5x); PAT Rs 8.63 cr to Rs 13.38 cr, down 17.1% in FY26 (p. 84)
Cumulative CFO/PAT -25.7%; receivables 211 closing days, Rs 14.10 cr outstanding 1-3 years (pp. 39, 86-87; Annex. 14)
Top-10 customers 83.58% of FY26 revenue, top-1 18.73%; Government share fell from 58.36% to 26.84% (pp. 49-50)
Related-party purchases and services Rs 14.11 cr (24.3% of purchases); related-party supplier advances Rs 8.06 cr (pp. 89-92)
Objects floor Rs 44.29 per share vs Rs 17.50 secondary price; blended fair value Rs 17.71 (Neutral)
Contracted growth: 20-year UP concession for 20 institutes and MoU for 50 AICTE labs; 30 labs already equipped (pp. 134-145)

issuers.sector: PET recycling (recycled polyester fibre, food-grade rPET resin, chemically recycled resin)
issuers.headline: Revenue grew at a 25.3% CAGR over FY24-FY26 with positive operating cash flow each year, but PAT was flat (Rs 211.3 m to Rs 224.9 m) and ROCE stayed near 10%; the Rs 90.10 reference price is about 69x FY26 EPS, in line with the single listed peer.
red_flags: Revenue CAGR 25.3% FY24-26; PAT flat at Rs 211.3 m / 205.7 m / 224.9 m (p. 72)
Operating cash flow positive every year; cumulative CFO/PAT 201%, about 108% after interest (p. 73)
ROCE 10.28% and EBITDA margin 10.86% FY26; net debt / EBITDA 3.40x, down from 5.25x (p. 122)
Capacity utilisation 70% in FY26 on 141,000 MTPA; 180,360 MTPA at Aug-2026 (pp. 24, 225)
Revaluation reserve Rs 614.81 m = 22.5% of total equity; issuer net worth excludes it (p. 397)
Customer and supplier concentration not disclosed; audit trail not enabled at database level (pp. 43-45, 244)
